authority: Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

description.en: Importer Exporter Code (IEC) is a 10-digit unique business identification number mandatory for any person importing or exporting goods and services from India. It is issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) and is required for customs clearance.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: All persons engaged in import or export of goods and services
verifiedConditions.claim: Any person or entity engaged in import or export of goods and services from India must obtain an IEC. This includes individuals, partnership firms, companies, LLPs, trusts, and HUFs.
A valid PAN (Permanent Account Number) is mandatory for obtaining an IEC. The IEC number is the same as the PAN of the applicant entity.

unverifiedEligibility: Government departments, charitable institutions, and certain persons importing/exporting for personal use may be exempt from IEC requirement.
IEC is not required for goods imported or exported for personal use not connected with trade or manufacture.
Defence and security establishments of the Government of India are exempted from IEC.
Certain categories of importers/exporters listed in Para 2.07 of the Foreign Trade Policy are exempt.

requirements.claim: PAN (Permanent Account Number) of the applicant entity is mandatory. The IEC number is the same as the PAN.
Aadhaar number of the proprietor, partner, director, or managing trustee is required for IEC application.
Bank account details of the applicant entity including cancelled cheque or bank certificate are required.
Address proof of the business premises such as electricity bill, rent agreement, or property deed is required.
Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) of the applicant or authorized signatory is required for online submission of the IEC application.
Photograph of the applicant (proprietor/partner/director) is required for the IEC application.

processInformation.claim: Register on the DGFT portal (dgft.gov.in) and create a user account using the entity's PAN and email address.
Fill the online application form ANF 2A (Aayaat Niryaat Form) with business details, PAN, Aadhaar, bank account details, and address of principal business premises.
Upload scanned copies of required documents including PAN card, Aadhaar card, cancelled cheque, address proof, and photograph.
Pay the application fee of Rs. 500 through net banking, debit card, or credit card on the DGFT portal.
Sign and submit the application using the Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) of the authorized signatory.
Upon successful processing, the IEC is generated and allotted. The IEC certificate can be downloaded from the DGFT portal. The IEC number is the same as the entity's PAN.

output.claim: An IEC certificate is issued electronically containing the 10-digit IEC number (same as PAN), entity name, address, and authorized signatories. The IEC is valid for lifetime and does not require renewal, but must be updated annually between April and June.

fees.applicability: New IEC application through the DGFT portal
fees.claim: The government fee for a new IEC application is Rs. 500, payable online through the DGFT portal.
No fee is charged for IEC modification or the mandatory annual update on the DGFT portal.

processingTime.applicability: New IEC application with complete documentation
processingTime.claim: IEC is typically issued within 1 to 3 working days of submitting the complete application with all required documents. In many cases, IEC is issued on the same day or next working day.

sources.title: DGFT Portal — IEC Application
sources.publisher: Directorate General of Foreign Trade, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The DGFT portal provides the online facility for IEC application, modification, and annual update. Form ANF 2A is the prescribed application form. Application fee is Rs. 500. Digital Signature Certificate is required for submission.
claimsSupported: IEC application is submitted online through the DGFT portal using Form ANF 2A.
PAN, Aadhaar, bank details, address proof, DSC, and photograph are required.
IEC is typically issued within 1-3 working days.
IEC certificate is available for download from the portal.
Annual update is mandatory between April and June.
sources.uncertainty: Processing times may vary based on document verification requirements and DGFT workload.

sources.title: Foreign Trade Policy 2023
sources.publisher: Directorate General of Foreign Trade, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: Chapter 2 of the Foreign Trade Policy 2023 prescribes the general provisions regarding IEC. Para 2.05 states that IEC shall be the PAN of the applicant. Para 2.07 lists exempted categories. Para 2.13 prescribes mandatory annual updation.
claimsSupported: IEC is mandatory for all persons importing or exporting goods and services.
IEC number is the same as the entity's PAN.
Certain categories are exempt from IEC requirement.
IEC has lifetime validity but requires mandatory annual update.
No fee for IEC modification or annual update.
sources.uncertainty: The Foreign Trade Policy is periodically updated and specific provisions may change.

limitations: This record covers new IEC registration for business entities only. Exemptions under Para 2.07 of the FTP are noted but not fully modeled.
The record does not cover IEC modification, suspension, or cancellation procedures in detail.
Star Export House and other export promotion council related IEC benefits are not covered.
The record does not cover customs clearance procedures that follow IEC issuance.
Branch-level IEC requirements for companies with multiple offices are not addressed.

review.reviewReason: Core IEC registration process is reviewed based on DGFT portal and FTP 2023, but exemption categories and export promotion benefits remain unmodeled.
nextReviewTrigger: Updates to the Foreign Trade Policy affecting IEC provisions.
Changes to the DGFT portal application process or fee structure.
New exemption categories added or removed from Para 2.07.
Changes to the mandatory annual update process.
